summary.headline: Dhanuka Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore; EBITDA Rs 55.01 crore and PAT Rs 36.30 crore, with FY27 growth guided to small single digits.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore from Rs 528.29 crore, with volume down about 12.7% and value down 12.56%, per management. Management attributed the quarter to delayed monsoon onset, a June rainfall deficit of about 40% (narrowing to 15% by end-July), weak herbicide demand in soybean and cotton states, and price erosion after a short-lived price hike. Management now expects a small single-digit growth in FY27 crop protection, versus the earlier guidance that was cut in the presentation. Biologicals, Bayer-acquired molecules and the Nagpur formulation plant (Rs 200 crore outlay, 23,000 MT) are the main forward-looking items.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from last three years' launches

segments.name: Zones (share of turnover)
segments.commentary: North 36%, West 37%, South 18%, East 9% of Q1 turnover.

segments.name: Product categories (share of turnover)
segments.commentary: Herbicides 42% (down about 25% YoY per analyst), Insecticides 25%, Fungicides 14% (up about 11% YoY per analyst; management did not dispute it, but confirmed the 14% share), Others 19%.

segments.name: Dahej chemical synthesis site
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 26 crore in Q1 vs Rs 16 crore last year; FY27 revenue guidance about Rs 65 crore; FY27 EBITDA expected at about negative Rs 4-5 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crop protection growth guided at a small single-digit rate (Rs 100-150 crore swing cited by analyst; management said small single-digit growth).
Management expects growth in Q2 and Q3 but said Q2 so far has not shown larger growth.
Five new launches planned in coming months: one liquid fertiliser, three fungicides, one herbicide.
Three biological products: two launched, third expected by end-August 2026; two more nutrition biologicals planned in FY27.
Bayer-acquired Iprovalicarb major revenue expected in September (grape season); not significant in FY27 balance sheet for overseas Bayer products.
Dahej EBITDA breakeven seen as difficult; expected negative Rs 4-5 crore for FY27.
Nagpur plant commissioning targeted Q4 FY28 (April 2028); capex about Rs 100 crore-plus in FY27-28 per CFO, with overall outlay up to Rs 200 crore.
Management expects no channel stocking or destocking by end of Q2.
Management said no Bayer-acquired product revenue booked in Q1 for overseas markets; company will address FY27 Bayer contribution separately.
Final dividend Rs 2 per share (100% of face value) approved at 41st AGM; record date and payment not stated.
capex_capacity: Nagpur (Butibori, Maharashtra): land acquired for a formulation plant, 23,000 MT per annum, outlay up to Rs 200 crore, operational by April 2028 (Q4 FY28 per later remark); CGST benefits from Maharashtra government.
Nagpur plant to be significantly automated; CFO indicated capex of about Rs 100 crore-plus in FY27-28; Dahej capex to be communicated later.
Dahej is a chemical synthesis facility in GIDC notified zone; management does not want formulation overlapping with synthesis, hence Nagpur is separate.
Company has four manufacturing facilities and 41 warehouses; reaches 10 million-plus farmers via about 6,500 distributors and 80,000-plus retailers.
Asset-turn assumption (7x-8x raised by analyst) not confirmed; management to revisit around late Q4 when project details are finalised.
Buyback of 5 lakh shares at Rs 1,400 per share absorbed Rs 70 crore; company described as debt-free.
demand_pricing: June rainfall deficit about 40%, narrowing to about 15% by end-July; management said even 1% deficit affects sowing areas.
Herbicide-heavy Q1 hit in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra (cotton/soybean) with some resowing; South also weak in June and July.
Price hike in April not sustained; prices declined from May, sharply in June and further in July per CFO, described as artificial due to war-related shortage.
Fungicide growth in Q1 attributed to a Japanese fungicide (Nissodium and Conika) on horticulture crops with high vegetable prices.
Management expects no stocking or destocking through end-Q2; channel inventory described as normal rotation after front-loading at end-FY26.
Biologicals: regulation seen favouring organised players as state governments tighten product approvals; prior-year base quarter had a ban with no sales.
Management benchmarks a minimum 20% margin on new launches; 9(3) and nutrition products carry materially higher margins.
Other expenses flat YoY despite 12.56% revenue decline; CFO said expenses are planned ahead of season.

qa_highlights.question: Why such a steep guidance cut, especially on top-line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is giving a realistic picture given monsoon movement; still hopeful of Q2 and Q3 growth, and the outlook was reset to small single-digit growth for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 200 crore Nagpur capex high for a formulation plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is designed to be significantly automated for safety and efficiency, so higher initial capex; asset turns to be addressed later (late Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Dahej split: revenue, EBITDA, Bayer revenue and royalty?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej revenue Rs 26 crore vs Rs 16 crore, EBITDA under Rs 1 crore vs Rs (-3) crore; Bayer product revenue not booked in Q1; royalty about Rs 4 crore, significantly lower YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory trend for Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees neither stocking nor destocking; inventory rotating normally with market demand; no change expected by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs price split for the revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said value -12.56% and volume about -12.7%, with price effect negligible; denied a 12% price growth in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 crop protection flattish given biologicals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small single-digit growth overall, after accounting for biologicals rebuilding in the year.
